Along each branch from T to P, the three identical resistors share the same voltage drop. U is located at the point in the upper branch after passing through two identical resistors, and Q is located at the point in the middle branch likewise after passing through two identical resistors, so U and Q have the same potential. The voltmeter connected between equipotential points reads zero.

method.method_draft: Use branch symmetry. From the image, identify that the upper branch from the left rail near T to the right rail near P contains three equal resistors in series, with W after the first resistor and U after the second. The middle branch from T to P also contains three equal resistors in series, with S after the first resistor and Q after the second. From the text, note that all resistors have the same resistance and the voltmeter has very high resistance, so connecting it does not alter the circuit. Since the two branches are identical resistor chains connected across the same two end nodes T and P, corresponding points along the chains are at the same potential. Therefore U and Q, both located after two equal resistor drops from T, are equipotential, so a voltmeter between Q and U reads zero.

method.method_draft: Assign potentials and calculate voltage division. From the image, take T and P as the two supply rails connected by the battery, with both the top and middle branches spanning from T to P. Each of these branches has three equal resistors in series. Let the potential difference between T and P be V. Because the resistors in each branch are equal, each resistor in a three-resistor branch drops V/3. In the top branch, W is one drop from T and U is two drops from T, so U is at T minus 2V/3. In the middle branch, S is one drop from T and Q is two drops from T, so Q is also at T minus 2V/3. Thus the potential difference between Q and U is zero, so the voltmeter would read zero between Q and U.
